editions.text: The station recorded 124 feeder visits, compared to the recent weekly average of 230. The species count dipped to 18 from the mean of 20. Tufted Titmice were the most frequent visitors, seen 64 times, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals following at 14 and 11 visits respectively. American Crows, Carolina Wrens, and Northern Cardinals provided the bulk of vocal detections. The day concluded with a Tufted Titmouse visiting 21 minutes before sunset, following its arrival 12 minutes before sunrise.

The morning opened with a Tufted Titmouse on the tube feeder six minutes before the 07:20 sunrise. So far, the station has logged 114 visits and 90 vocalizations. Carolina Wrens dominated the early hour with 34 detections, their songs filling the air before the visual traffic peaked with 46 Tufted Titmouse sightings.

As the light fully arrived, House Finches and Mourning Doves joined the regulars. By 10:30, the chorus had shifted slightly, with American Crows and Eastern Towhees providing background noise as the initial rush of Tufted Titmice and Cardinals subsided. The last confirmed visitor arrived at the feeder around 09:50.

Thirteen species have been recorded against the recent mean of 17.

The midday traffic remains steady, with 238 feeder visits logged by 15:30, well above the recent seven-day average of 168. Tufted Titmice continue to hold the tube feeder, accounting for 120 of those visits, while Northern Cardinals and House Finches make up the bulk of the remaining regulars. The weather is wet, with 24.9 mm of precipitation recorded so far under a high of 22.2 C, though the wind has remained light at 4 kph.

A Cedar Waxwing appeared at the feeder, marking a return after seven days away since its last record on September 15. It was one of two probable sightings alongside a Gray Catbird.

Vocal detections are currently quieter than the recent average, with 177 heard against a mean of 221. Eastern Towhees provided the most frequent background calls in the afternoon, totaling 30 detections, while a Red-shouldered Hawk was heard three times during the 14:00 hour. The last visual record is a Tufted Titmouse, seen 490 minutes after sunrise.
